decisions.why: Distinct dated first-party 2015/2017 creator and publication event counts, 2019 catalog announcement, and October 2026 filter snapshot retain their year and distinct event/stock units.
decisions.unresolved: A comparable longitudinal paid-publisher sales census has not been established.

decisions.why: Two attributed game developer reports separate first-period cash receipts, operational/living costs, refunds and approximate labor; arithmetic examples are marked illustrations rather than audited net income.
decisions.unresolved: Platformwide owner labor-adjusted profit distribution and each game's final audited profit are unavailable.

decisions.why: Dated July 2025 indexing and payment-processor events are recorded as distinct, scoped platform actions; official rules do not become estimated affected seller populations or lost sales.
decisions.unresolved: The chance of an ordinary product being deindexed or denied payment and contemporary affected populations remain unmeasured.

decisions.why: The fixed ledger enforces required cited evidence paths, progress/status consistency and explicit unknown market measures; private API transaction records and public metadata remain separate evidence classes.
decisions.unresolved: Accepting research design and source classification does not count missing paid buyer transactions as collected.

decisions.why: An actual developer-disclosed settlement and fee waterfall is arithmetically reconciled as far as the evidence permits; an unexplained 23-cent mismatch is retained alongside platform/refund/processor rules.
decisions.unresolved: Publisher's complete ledger, final tax, labor cost and profit cannot be inferred from an individual gross payout.

decisions.why: An operational eligibility rule defines first mandatory-positive-price commercial titles and requires aligned 30-, 90- and 365-day seller cohorts, including zero-paid and delisted titles.
decisions.unresolved: No probability sample of the defined real first-time paid-game cohorts, or their mean/median return, was acquired.

decisions.why: A test-verified accounting contract distinguishes captured paid orders, nonoverlapping refunded orders, fully reversed disputes, retained units, processor/platform costs and final cash under explicit hypothetical inputs.
decisions.unresolved: The 2026 live rate of refunds, merchant chargeback costs, retained orders and representative net proceeds remains unknown.

rule: Do not conflate accepted operational and evidence-classification tasks with representative empirical income estimates.
